submission.natural_language_explanation: L0/N1109+ is a token-level detector for the word SUPPORT: at any position whose token is a common surface form of it (' support', ' supports', ' supported', ' Support', 'supporting', 'supportive') the pole fires near its maximum, whatever the sense (financial, emotional, structural, military, software), part of speech, case or surrounding text - a nonsense sentence around the token fires it as hard as a real one (3.25), while stem-free synonyms of support (help, aid, assistance, backing, fund, endorse, sponsor) give nothing. Its key is one linear direction in the token embedding, so the same pole also fires at about two-thirds strength on the token embeddings nearest 'support' - the 'supported platforms'/compatibility register (platform(s), Windows, Mac, PC, Linux, OS, iOS, Android, PlayStation, Xbox, USB, native, compatible, can, allows, able) and 'social' - but not on words that merely contain the letters (' suppose', ' supply', ' Supporter') and only weakly on rare merged forms of the lemma (' Supporters'); its output write is flat (Jacobian kurtosis 3.4, 0% lens agreement, max direct unembedding projection 0.25), so it reacts to what has been read rather than preparing an upcoming token.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Residents of the coastal district spent the spring repairing the seawall, clearing storm drains and replanting the dunes above the high-water line. The council approved a modest budget, volunteers organised weekend crews, and local shops donated tools, gloves and refreshments. Engineers warned that the work would take several years and that a single storm could undo most of it. Even so, attendance at the monthly meetings grew, and the mood in the village shifted from resignation to something closer to determination. In a letter read aloud at the closing session, the mayor thanked everyone who had given time, money or expertise, and asked the assembly to support the next phase of the project before winter.
